messages:
maya: Heads up — a handful of jobs hitting model-serving in eu-west-1 started failing around 10:12 UTC. Errors are connection resets to the S3 interface endpoint (vpce-0a9f1c2e). Not DNS timeouts, immediate RST. Anyone seen this?
kevin: Which VPCE and which ENIs? Can you paste ENI IPs + SGs? :thinking: 
nishant: Also check source/dest check and any recent routing changes. We had a TGW change earlier.
maya: VPCE is vpce-0a9f1c2e — ENIs in subnets subnet-aaa (10.0.5.12) and subnet-bbb. Endpoint SG is sg-ep-eu, target model nodes SG is sg-models. AWS flow logs show SYN, SYN-ACK, then RST from the node side.
olivia: Route tables look normal for that private RTB. FYI interface endpoints don’t need route entries but if traffic is SNAT'd via NAT/proxy it can get asymmetric. Any recent proxy/gwlb changes?
maya: Here's tcpdump from a node: ```tcpdump -nni eth0 'host 10.0.5.12' -c 10
10:12:34.123 IP 10.0.4.21.42624 > 10.0.5.12.443: SYN
10:12:34.124 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 10.0.4.21.42624: SYN, ACK
10:12:34.125 IP 10.0.4.21.42624 > 10.0.5.12.443: RST
```
kevin: Node sending RST after SYN-ACK usually means kernel closed socket because of asymmetric route or conntrack/iptables. Check `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter` and conntrack. Any recent CNI or kernel updates?
nishant: I see automation installed a new weave/cni package earlier today on that image. Also cloud-init shows a recent change to route propagation in the TGW attachment (change ch-7789).
olivia: DNS from nodes resolves to endpoint IP: `dig s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` -> 10.0.5.12 (endpoint). From bastion the endpoint responds to curl, from nodes it fails. Bastion and nodes are in different AZs.
maya: I checked `ip route` on the node — default points at a NAT GW in the same subnet (looks like SNAT path). If packets head to ENI then back via NAT path, rp_filter may drop.
kevin: Exactly. If replies come back on an interface different from the one the kernel expects, rp_filter will drop and kernel can reset sockets. Run `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter`.
maya: rp_filter is 1 on these nodes. I toggled to 0 on a test node and endpoint connections work immediately.
nishant: Why was rp_filter 1? Our baseline AMI enables it. But the route change via TGW likely introduced asymmetric routing for that AZ.
olivia: There was a TGW change earlier that preferred a route through a firewall appliance in that AZ — that could be the asymmetry. I'll roll that back.
maya: Action items: 1) roll rp_filter=0 to a small subset of the eu-west1 GPU pool (nishant) 2) rollback the TGW/route change (olivia) 3) add a scale/health test that validates endpoint DNS + direct ENI connectivity on scale events (kevin) 4) document endpoint SG expectations and add an alert for asymmetric routes. I will open the config PR.
deploy-bot: Deployment NOTE: rollback of change id ch-7789 scheduled for 1987654400, initiated by olivia.
kevin: :thumbsup: Also watch cost — autoscaler spiked extra GPUs during the issue window. If we push image changes to turn off rp_filter at boot, schedule in a maintenance window so we don't burn dev credits.
nishant: I'll run a rolling change on 10% of nodes and post results here.
maya: Tested on one node — after rp_filter=0, pods can reach S3 via the interface endpoint, logs no longer show RSTs. Monitoring for 30m.
olivia: I'll confirm TGW rollback completed and post update. Thanks team :pray:
